status: frozen after the first two wide zoos (2-384-1: 27.4 dB; 2-1024-1 pending) and the least-squares ceiling check, before the parameter sweep
question: What does dictionary-level programmability cost in representation quality? A SIREN with one sine layer and a linear readout is exactly programmable for Gaussian blur (stage 02); a deep SIREN is not. At matched parameter counts, how far behind is the shallow family, and is the gap a capacity limit of the dictionary or an optimisation limit?

already_known_when_frozen.shallow ceilings: With the first layer fixed, the least-squares readout reaches 21.0 / 23.6 / 27.3 dB for W = 32 / 64 / 384 trained frequencies, equal to the trained zoo PSNR (20.9 / 23.6 / 27.3): training has converged, the dictionary is the limit. Random (untrained) frequencies give 12.6 / 14.6 / 23.3 / 24.3 dB for W = 32 / 64 / 384 / 1024.
already_known_when_frozen.reference: The best k DCT coefficients of the same images give 23.6 / 29.1 / 34.2 / 40.4 dB for k = 128 / 256 / 384 / 512: even an ideal orthogonal plane-wave dictionary needs about 500 terms for 40 dB, while 2-32-32-1 (1,185 weights) reaches 61.5 dB and 2-32-32-32-1 reaches 74.0 dB.
already_known_when_frozen.consequence: Width cannot substitute for depth here; programmability of the dictionary layer has a large price for a standalone image INR.

sweep.recipe: MNIST test 0..19, 2,000 Adam steps at 1e-3, NumPy trainer; plus 5 networks of 2-384-1 at 10,000 steps as the optimisation control
sweep.metric: fit PSNR of the clipped rendering against the MNIST image; blur_1 programmability from stage 02's exact (shallow) and input-attenuation (deep) programs on the function-space target

predictions_frozen_before_running.W1_gap_at_matched_params: At about 1,000-1,500 weights the deep family exceeds the shallow family by more than 25 dB median PSNR (2-32-32-1 vs 2-256-1 and 2-384-1).
predictions_frozen_before_running.W2_shallow_saturates: Shallow PSNR grows by less than 4 dB per doubling of W beyond 256, and 2-1024-1 stays below 32 dB.
predictions_frozen_before_running.W3_optimisation_is_not_the_limit: 2-384-1 trained for 10,000 steps improves by less than 1 dB over 2,000 steps.
predictions_frozen_before_running.W4_deep_small_beats_shallow_large: 2-16-16-1 (321 weights) exceeds 2-1024-1 (4,097 weights) in median PSNR.
predictions_frozen_before_running.W5_programmability_unchanged: Every shallow network in the sweep keeps the exact blur program below 1e-6 MSE against the function-space target; no deep network in the sweep gets the input-attenuation program below 0.7 x no-edit.

interpretation: If W1-W5 hold: for standalone image INRs, exact dictionary-level programmability costs tens of dB at equal parameter count, because compression comes from composition (harmonics), which is exactly what breaks programmability. The place where programmability is cheap is a conditional INR whose capacity lives in an encoder (the arbitrary-scale SR decoders of the footprint study: a local Fourier field with linear readout matched LTE within 0.10 dB at symmetric scales) -- a prediction for the stage that follows the ICME submission, not a result of this stage.
